title: The Great Migration, Month by Month
excerpt: Where are the herds of the Great Migration in each month? A month-by-month overview to help you plan your safari.
body:
The Great Migration is the year-round movement of very large numbers of wildebeest, together with zebras and gazelles, through the Serengeti–Mara ecosystem. They follow rain and fresh grass. Exact timing varies each year, so this is a general guide.

## January–March: southern Serengeti and Ndutu

The herds graze on the short-grass plains. Calving peaks around February. See [Ndutu and calving](/blog/ndutu-calving-season/).

## April–May: moving through the centre

With the long rains, the herds start moving northwest through central Serengeti. See [April and May](/blog/great-migration-april-may/).

## June: Western Corridor

Many herds move into the Western Corridor and cross the Grumeti River. See [June](/blog/great-migration-june-grumeti/).

## July–October: northern Serengeti and Masai Mara

The herds reach the north and cross the Mara River, sometimes back and forth. See [July to October](/blog/great-migration-july-october/).

## November–December: back south

With the short rains, the herds move south again through the eastern and central Serengeti. See [November and December](/blog/great-migration-november-december/).

## Important

Nature does not follow a calendar. A good guide and flexible planning increase your chances.

Read our [Great Migration page](/great-wildebeest-migration/) or [plan your migration safari](/travel-proposal/).
